text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has exempted oil and gas exploration and production companies from the payment of import duty, sales tax and regulatory duty on machinery, equipment, materials, specialised vehicles, accessories, spares, chemicals and consumables which are not manufactured locally.
- The government has decided to auction the properties of defaulters of banks and financial institutions to recover 140 billion rupees of non-performing loans.
- Privatisation Commission Khawaja Muhammad Asif chairman is due to visit Dubai to meet potential investors and offer them 49 percent of the shares of the Pak Arab Refinery Co.
- Pakistan strongly denied reports about interference by its Inter-Services Intelligence in Afghanistan's internal affairs.
- The government increased regulatory duty on polyester fibre to 10 percent from five percent effective May 28.
- Total fresh taxes in the 1997/98 (July-June) budget will not exceed 10 billion rupees, says Hafizullah Ishaque, chairman of the Central Board of Revenue.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said there would be no unnecessary retrenchment of employees.
- The government has set up a supreme body, the Federal Ehtesab (accountability) Council to implement the concept of accountability committees at grass-roots level.

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told the Senate (upper house) that a sizeable number of employees in government departments and corporations would be shifted to surplus pool to downsize these institutions.
- A large number of Afghan nationals living in Pakistan are going back to reinforce Taleban troops in their crucial offensive against rival forces in northern Afghanistan.
- The government is considering a proposal to hold a referendum on renaming North Western Frontier Province.
